relationships.subject: TRPM8
relationships.evidence_quote: TRPM8 activation is known to block capsaicin-induced TRPV1 activity in human corneal, conjunctival epithelial cells, and stromal cells.

relationships.subject: VEGF-A
relationships.evidence_quote: Inflammatory factor, VEGF-A-induced TRPV1 activity, was blocked by TRPM8 activation.

relationships.subject: TRPV1
relationships.evidence_quote: blocking TRPV1 activity led to reduction of mRNA expression of Nav1.7 and NaV1.8, in DED animals when compared to controls

relationships.subject: TRPV1
relationships.evidence_quote: blocking TRPV1 activity led to reduction of mRNA expression of Nav1.7 and NaV1.8, in DED animals when compared to controls

relationships.subject: Nav1.8
relationships.evidence_quote: optogenetic inhibition of Nav1.8 expressing corneal afferents resulted in the decreased of DED related pain

relationships.subject: TRPV1
relationships.evidence_quote: TRPV1 activation in human corneal epithelial cells is known to secrete proinflammatory factors like IL-6 and IL-8.

relationships.subject: muscimol
relationships.evidence_quote: Use of GABAA receptor agonist, muscimol, resulted in the reduction of hypertonic saline induced orbicularis oculi muscle activity in DED animals

relationships.subject: P2X7R
relationships.evidence_quote: P2X7R blockade using an antagonistic or expression knockdown resulted in reduced mRNA expression of P2X7R and P2X4R, along with reduction in the hypertonic saline-induced orbicularis oculi muscle activity in DED animals

key_findings: Review: increased expression or activity of TRPA1, TRPV1, Nav1.8, KCNJ6, ASIC1, ASIC3, P2X, P2Y and NMDA receptors is implicated in dry eye disease pathogenesis, whereas TRPM8, GABAA receptor, CFTR and NKA activity is associated with resolution.
TRPM8 activation blocks TRPV1 activity (including VEGF-A-induced) in ocular surface cells, and TRPV1 blockade reduces Nav1.7/Nav1.8 expression in DED models.
